name: Bosutinib (CML, chronic phase, first-line)

biomarkers.note: CML is defined by the BCR::ABL1 fusion (Philadelphia chromosome); confirm Ph-positive or BCR::ABL1-positive by qPCR at diagnosis. A T315I kinase-domain mutation confers resistance to bosutinib (and to imatinib, dasatinib and nilotinib); ponatinib or asciminib is the treatment option for T315I. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Chronic Myeloid Leukemia v2.2027.

lineOfTherapy: first-line for newly diagnosed chronic-phase CML (a second-generation TKI)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: BCR::ABL1-positive (Ph-positive) chronic-phase CML confirmed by qPCR
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2027, CML workup (Ph-positive or BCR::ABL1 positive by qPCR)

drugs.name: Bosutinib

provenance.locator: MS-26 (recommended starting dose of bosutinib is 400 mg daily for newly diagnosed CP-CML)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Chronic Myeloid Leukemia v2.2027, MS-26. Bosutinib 400 mg PO once daily for newly diagnosed CP-CML (better tolerated than the 500 mg dose used in later-line settings). Some experts start at 200 to 300 mg once daily with escalation to improve gastrointestinal tolerability, reserving 400 mg initiation for high-risk disease (MS-26). Take with food. Avoid proton-pump inhibitors and H2 blockers. Days 1 to 28 represents continuous daily dosing; continue until loss of response, progression or intolerance.

supportiveCare: Continuous daily oral therapy taken with food; avoid proton-pump inhibitors and H2 blockers (reduced absorption).
Bosutinib commonly causes gastrointestinal toxicity (diarrhea); a lower starting dose with escalation can improve tolerability (MS-26).
Monitor BCR::ABL1 (IS) by qPCR at milestones; if resistance, test for kinase-domain mutations (T315I directs ponatinib or asciminib).

monitoring: CBC with differential at baseline and periodically
BCR::ABL1 (IS) by qPCR at approximately 3, 6 and 12 months and periodically thereafter (CML-G)
assessment of diarrhea and fluid/renal status

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 to 4 diarrhea, hepatotoxicity or other toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Interrupt for significant toxicity and resume at a reduced dose per prescribing information; treatment with a lower bosutinib dose (400 mg or less daily) reduces drug-related adverse events (MS-26). Physician decides.

guideline.locator: MS-26 (recommended starting dose of bosutinib is 400 mg daily for newly diagnosed CP-CML; 200 to 300 mg start with escalation for tolerability; 400 mg start for high-risk disease); PPI/H2 blocker avoidance (CML-D); T315I/ponatinib option (manuscript and CML footnote)
